name: Ohio
overview: Ohio mostly sells tax-delinquent real estate outright after a tax foreclosure. A court orders the parcel sold, and the county sheriff sells it, usually online through the state's sheriff sale auction site run by RealAuction under a state contract. In a tax foreclosure the minimum bid can be the taxes, assessments, penalties, interest and costs owed rather than the usual two-thirds of appraised value. Parcels left unsold after two sales are forfeited to the state, and the county auditor can later offer them at a forfeited land sale. Some county treasurers also sell tax certificates (liens): at a public auction, bidding starts at 18% simple interest per year and goes down. Some counties, such as Franklin, instead sell their certificates in bulk as a portfolio.

counties.how_to_bid: Monthly delinquent tax sales are in person. The minimum bid covers the taxes owed through the sale date plus case costs, not other lien holders' amounts. The winning bidder pays a 10% deposit to the Treasurer's Office by 4:30 P.M. on sale day (cashier's or certified check) and the balance within 30 days of the filing of the confirmation of sale; bring the name for the deed, a tax mailing address, a phone number and ID. A sale with no bids is rescheduled to the first Tuesday of the following month. Tax certificate foreclosures (private attorney) are sold online through RealAuction: register there and post a $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 deposit per property by wire or ACH before the Monday auction. Sales are as is, and properties are not open for inspection.

counties.how_to_bid: All sheriff sales have been online through RealAuction since April 2022. A deposit is paid to RealAuction at least 48 business hours before the sale: $2,000 for appraised value of $10,000 or less, $5,000 for over $10,000 and under $200,000, $10,000 over $200,000. A Purchaser Information Sheet must accompany each bid. Tax foreclosures filed by the County Treasurer have a minimum bid set by court order (other sales start at two-thirds of appraised value), and liens other than the taxes foreclosed may survive the sale. The balance is due by certified bank check within 30 days after the Sheriff contacts the buyer following confirmation. No entry to the property without a court order.

counties.how_to_bid: Register with RealAuction (including the Purchaser Information Form) and bid online on the county's sheriff sale site; auctions begin at 11:00 a.m. Eastern on Wednesdays. Deposits are $2,000 (appraised $1 to $10,000), $5,000 ($10,001 to $200,000) or $10,000 (over $200,000), by bank wire (due 5 p.m. two business days before) or ACH (due 4 p.m. five business days before); no cash. The balance is due at confirmation, which typically takes up to 30 days. Minimum bid is not stated.

counties.how_to_bid: Tax sales are held in person at the Clark County Commission Chambers, 5th floor of the Municipal Court Building. Bids begin at the minimum bid unless the court directs otherwise; the winning bidder pays the full amount plus 1.5% poundage at the end of the sale, in cash or by check. All sales are 'buyer beware'. The Sheriff prepares the deed after the Clerk's confirmation, about two to four weeks later. Deposit and registration rules are not stated. Other (non-tax) real estate sales are linked to the Ohio sheriff sale auction site.

counties.how_to_bid: Delinquent tax sales are held in person at the Wood County Courthouse, One Courthouse Square, Bowling Green, at 10:00 AM on the listed date. For a tax sale the deposit is 10% of the starting bid, but no less than $1,000.00, paid to the Sheriff's Deputy by personal or certified check once the day's sales are completed; the remainder is due in 30 to 90 days. A buyer who cannot complete the purchase may be cited for contempt of court. Bank foreclosures are sold separately online through RealAuction. Registration rules for tax sales are not stated.
